book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 3 · Illness and Injury Prevention
title: Preventing Injury: What the PCP Sees and Does

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you've treated many injuries after they happened. Today, as a PCP:

  1. The three levels of prevention, and why paramedics matter
  2. The tools: four Es, passive protection, the Haddon matrix
  3. Turning calls into prevention: teachable moments, PCR data, safety

Textbook: Chapter 3, PDF pages 179–218
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you've treated plenty of injuries, but always after they happened. This chapter asks a different question: how could this injury have been prevented? Paramedics see what hospital staff never see: the broken stair, the sharp curve, the corner where crashes keep happening. Today we'll cover three things. First, the three levels of prevention, and why paramedics matter. Second, the main tools: the four Es, passive protection, and the Haddon matrix. Third, how you, as a PCP, turn ordinary calls into prevention, with teachable moments, good documentation, and safe habits, including on overdose calls.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你处理过很多伤害，但都是在伤害发生之后。本章问一个不同的问题：这个伤害本来可以怎样预防？院前急救员能看到医院的人永远看不到的东西：坏掉的楼梯、危险的弯道、车祸一再发生的路口。今天讲三件事：第一，预防的三个层级，以及院前急救员为什么重要；第二，主要工具：四个 E、被动保护和 Haddon 矩阵；第三，作为 PCP，怎样把日常出车变成预防：可教时机、好的记录和安全习惯，包括在药物过量现场。

slides.title: Three levels of prevention
slides.body:
Primarystop the injury happeningkeep it from ever occurring
Secondarylimit harm after it happenswhere EMS has always worked
Tertiaryrehabilitationrecovery after injury

1996: primary prevention called essential for every EMS system. 2011 NOCP added health promotion and public safety (8.1a, 8.1b).
slides.say: Prevention comes in three levels. Primary prevention keeps an injury from ever happening. Secondary prevention reduces the harm of an injury that has already happened. That's where EMS has always worked: every time you control bleeding or splint a fracture. Tertiary prevention is rehabilitation afterwards. In 1996, a consensus statement called primary prevention essential for every EMS system, and the 2011 NOCP for paramedics added health promotion and public safety. Why paramedics? You're spread across every community, you reflect the people you serve, you're trusted and welcome in schools, and because you see injuries every day, people listen to you.
slides.sayZh: 预防分三个层级。一级预防让伤害根本不发生。二级预防减轻已经发生的伤害的后果，这是 EMS 一直以来的工作：每次止血、固定骨折都是。三级预防是之后的康复。1996 年，一份共识声明称一级预防是每个 EMS 系统必不可少的工作；2011 年版院前急救员 NOCP 也新增了健康促进与公共安全。为什么是院前急救员？你们分布在每个社区，反映着所服务人群的构成，受人信任，学校也欢迎你们；而且因为每天都看到伤害的后果，人们愿意听你们说。

slides.title: Injury in Canada: the numbers
slides.body:
Injury in CanadaFigure
Injury deaths, 201616,527
Suicide / transport / falls24% / 21% / 18%
Poisoning / homicide9% / 3%
Admissions, unintentional injuryabout 200,000
Cost, unintentional injuryover $16 billion

Falls lead injuries that kill or need a hospital stay. Years of potential life lost = 65 − age at death.
slides.say: In 2016, sixteen thousand five hundred twenty-seven Canadians died from injuries: twenty-four percent by suicide, twenty-one percent in transport, eighteen percent from falls, nine percent from poisoning, and three percent by homicide. Unintentional injuries account for about two hundred thousand hospital admissions and cost more than sixteen billion dollars. They're the leading cause of death for males aged one to forty-five and females aged one to twenty-four. Falls are the top cause of injuries that kill or need a hospital stay. And years of potential life lost is sixty-five minus the age at death, so a twenty-year-old killed in a crash loses forty-five years.
slides.sayZh: 2016 年，加拿大有一万六千五百二十七人死于伤害：自杀占百分之二十四，交通百分之二十一，跌倒百分之十八，中毒百分之九，他杀百分之三。非故意伤害造成约二十万次住院，花费超过一百六十亿加元。它是一到四十五岁男性、一到二十四岁女性的首位死因。跌倒是导致死亡或需要住院的伤害的首要原因。潜在寿命损失年等于六十五减去死亡年龄，所以一个二十岁的人死于车祸，损失四十五年。

slides.title: The four Es of prevention
slides.body:
The EExample
EducationTeach seniors to clear trip hazards
EnforcementLegislation, regulation, litigation
Engineering / environmentGuardrails, child-resistant caps
Economic incentivesInsurance discounts, free helmets

The strongest programs combine all four.
slides.say: The four Es are your main toolbox. Education teaches people about a risk and tries to change their behaviour, like teaching seniors to clear trip hazards. Knowing a risk doesn't always change behaviour, but education paves the way for the other Es. Enforcement has three forms: legislation, laws passed by elected bodies; regulation, rules from agencies on how products are made, sold, or used; and litigation, lawsuits that push makers to fix dangerous products. Engineering, or environment, changes the design of a product or place, like guardrails or child-resistant caps. Economic incentives use money, like insurance discounts or free helmets. The strongest programs combine all four.
slides.sayZh: 四个 E 是主要的工具箱。教育：让人了解风险，努力改变行为，比如教老人清除绊倒隐患。知道风险不一定会改变行为，但教育能为其他几个 E 铺路。执法有三种形式：立法，由民选机构制定的法律；法规，由政府机构制定、管控产品如何制造、销售或使用的规则；诉讼，通过起诉迫使厂商改进危险产品。工程或环境：改变产品或场所的设计，比如护栏、儿童安全瓶盖。经济激励：用钱推动，比如保险优惠或免费头盔。最有效的项目会把四个 E 结合起来。

slides.title: Passive protection works best
slides.body:
The less effort it takes, the more likely it works

  • Active: the person must act every time (buckle up)
  • Passive (automatic protection): works 24 hours a day
  • Examples: sprinklers, air bags, soft playground surfaces
  • Still teach: air bags don't replace seat belts
slides.say: Here's one of the most testable ideas in the chapter. Active interventions need people to do something every single time, like buckling up. Passive interventions, also called automatic protection, protect people without any decision. Passive ones are often the most successful, because they work twenty-four hours a day: sprinklers in buildings, air bags in cars, soft surfaces under playground equipment. The rule of thumb is simple: the less personal effort required, the more likely it works. But education still matters. People need to know, for example, that an air bag doesn't replace a seat belt.
slides.sayZh: 这是本章最常考的观点之一。主动干预需要人每一次都去做，比如系安全带。被动干预，也叫自动保护，不需要任何决定就能保护人。被动干预往往最成功，因为它全天二十四小时都在起作用：楼里的喷淋系统、车里的气囊、游乐设施下面的软地面。经验法则很简单：个人需要付出的努力越少，越可能成功。但教育仍然重要：人们需要知道，比如气囊不能代替安全带。

slides.q: Your service wants to cut poisonings of toddlers by household medicines. Which intervention is most likely to work?
options: Posters asking parents to store pills up high
A pamphlet handed out at baby clinics
A radio ad about poison safety
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. Your service wants to cut poisonings of toddlers by household medicines. Which intervention is most likely to work? A, posters asking parents to store pills up high. B, child-resistant caps on medicine bottles. C, a pamphlet handed out at baby clinics. D, a radio ad about poison safety. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你所在的机构想减少幼儿误服家用药物中毒。哪项干预最可能有效？A 张贴海报提醒家长把药放高处；B 药瓶使用儿童安全瓶盖；C 在婴儿诊所发宣传册；D 播放关于防中毒的电台广告。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A child-resistant cap is a passive, engineering intervention: it protects the child automatically, without parents having to remember anything each time. A, C, and D are all education. Education is useful and helps build support for change, but it relies on people changing their behaviour every day, so on its own it's usually less effective.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。儿童安全瓶盖属于被动的工程类干预：它自动保护孩子，不需要家长每次都记得做什么。A、C、D 都属于教育。教育有用，也能为改变争取支持，但它依赖人们每天改变行为，所以单靠教育通常效果较差。

slides.title: The Haddon matrix: adding time
slides.body:
Public health model: host (person), agent (what injures), environment. Haddon added time: 3 × 3 = 9 cells.

Pre-eventstop it happeninge.g. handrails, better lighting
Eventreduce injury as it happense.g. helmet, seat belt, soft surface
Post-eventreduce harm afterwardse.g. fast 9-1-1 call, prehospital care
slides.say: The public health model looks at the host, the person who gets hurt; the agent, what causes the injury; and the environment where it happens. William Haddon added time: pre-event, event, and post-event. Three factors times three phases gives nine cells. Take an older adult falling on stairs. Pre-event, add handrails and better lighting. During the event, something that softens the impact helps. Post-event, a fast call for help and good prehospital care. Notice that your usual work sits in the post-event column. The matrix pushes you past more education or blame, toward practical, measurable fixes.
slides.sayZh: 公共卫生模型看三样东西：宿主，也就是受伤的人；致病因子，也就是造成伤害的东西；以及伤害发生的环境。William Haddon 加入了时间：事件前、事件中、事件后。三个因素乘三个时相，就是九格。以老人在楼梯上跌倒为例：事件前，加扶手、改善照明；事件中，能缓冲撞击的东西有帮助；事件后，是迅速呼救和良好的院前急救。注意，你平时的工作就在事件后这一栏。这个矩阵推动你越过「多做宣教」或「怪某个人」，去找实际、可测量的解决办法。

slides.title: Surveillance starts with your PCR
slides.body:
Injury surveillance: ongoing, systematic collection, analysis and use of injury data

  • Know who is hurt, where, and by what mechanism
  • Headlines mislead: everyday falls often matter more
  • PCR: scene details and the external mechanism
  • PCR: the nature of the injury
  • PCR: safety devices used or not (belt, helmet, car seat)
slides.say: Injury surveillance is the ongoing, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of injury data, and its final step is using that data to prevent injuries. You need to know who is getting hurt, where, and by what mechanism. The news may focus on one dramatic crash, while the data show that ordinary falls in older people are a bigger, more fixable threat. For paramedics, surveillance starts with the patient care report. Record the scene, the external mechanism, the nature of the injury, and whether a seat belt, helmet, or car seat was used, accurately and legibly. With standardized coding, your reports can reveal trends.
slides.sayZh: 伤害监测是指持续、系统地收集、分析和解读伤害数据，最后一环是用这些数据来预防伤害。你需要知道谁在受伤、在哪里、通过什么机制受伤。新闻可能盯着一起惊人的车祸，而数据显示，老人日常跌倒才是更大、也更容易解决的威胁。对院前急救员来说，监测从病人护理报告开始：准确、清楚地记录现场情况、外部致伤机制、伤情性质，以及是否使用了安全带、头盔或儿童座椅。有了标准化编码，你的报告就能揭示趋势。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Treat the injury: secondary prevention
  • Model safety: seat belt, PPE, safe lifting
  • Point out a hazard tactfully
  • Report suspected abuse or neglect

PCP adds

  • Health promotion is a paramedic NOCP competency
  • Spots patterns: same place, same injury
  • Uses teachable moments with a specific fix
  • Documents for data: mechanism, injuries, safety devices
  • Sets the standard the crew will copy
slides.say: Every licence level does secondary prevention by treating the injury, models safe habits like seat belts and PPE, points out hazards politely, and reports suspected abuse or neglect. The right side is what the paramedic role adds. Health promotion and injury prevention are written into the paramedic NOCP, so they're part of your professional competencies. You're expected to notice patterns, like the same intersection or the same kind of fall, and explain them to others. You use teachable moments with a specific fix. You document so your reports become useful data. And the textbook reminds new paramedics that your habits filter down to your crew.
slides.sayZh: 每个执照级别都要做的是：通过处置伤害做二级预防，以身作则系安全带、用 PPE，礼貌地指出隐患，上报疑似虐待或忽视。右栏是院前急救员角色多出来的部分。健康促进和伤害预防写进了院前急救员的 NOCP，是你职业能力的一部分。你要能发现规律，比如同一个路口、同一类跌倒，并向别人解释。你要利用可教时机，给出具体的办法。你的记录要能成为有用的数据。书里还提醒新的院前急救员：你的习惯会传给你的队员。

slides.title: The teachable moment
slides.body:
Right after a close call, people listen best.

  1. The person is receptive now (respect culture and religion)
  2. The setting allows a non-judgemental, non-embarrassing message
  3. There's a specific fix: belt, car seat, helmet, locked firearm

Praise works best: "Your helmet did its job today."
slides.say: A teachable moment is a time when people are especially open to advice, often right after a near miss, when they suddenly feel how vulnerable they were. Three conditions make it work. First, the person can take the message in right now, and you adjust for cultural and religious differences. Second, the setting lets you say it without threatening, judging, or embarrassing anyone. Third, there's a clear, specific fix, like a seat belt, a properly installed car seat, a helmet, or a locked firearm; vague advice doesn't stick. Timing matters: lecturing parents right after their child is badly hurt won't help. And praise works best.
slides.sayZh: 可教时机是指人们特别愿意听取建议的时刻，常常是刚躲过一劫、突然意识到自己多么脆弱的时候。要成功需要三个条件。第一，对方此刻听得进去，而且你会顾及文化和宗教差异。第二，场合允许你不带威胁、不评判、不让人难堪地说。第三，有一个清楚具体的办法，比如系安全带、正确安装的儿童座椅、头盔、上锁的枪支；含糊的建议记不住。时机很重要：孩子刚受重伤就训斥家长，不会有用。表扬的效果最好。

slides.q: A teenager has minor scrapes after falling off his bike. He wasn't wearing a helmet. He's calm and chatting with you. What's the best approach?
options: Say nothing, because prevention isn't part of your job
Calmly explain how a helmet would protect his head next time
Wait for his mother and tell her she should supervise him better
Write "irresponsible, no helmet" in the patient care report
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A teenager has minor scrapes after falling off his bike. He wasn't wearing a helmet. He's calm and chatting with you. What's the best approach? A, say nothing, because prevention isn't part of your job. B, calmly explain how a helmet would protect his head next time. C, wait for his mother and tell her she should supervise him better. D, write irresponsible, no helmet, in the patient care report. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一个少年骑车摔倒，只有轻微擦伤。他没戴头盔，情绪平静，正和你聊天。最好的做法是什么？A 什么也不说，因为预防不是你的工作；B 平静地解释下次戴头盔怎样保护他的头；C 等他妈妈来，告诉她应该看好孩子；D 在病人护理报告里写「不负责任，没戴头盔」。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. This is a teachable moment: he's receptive, the setting is calm, and there's a specific fix, a helmet. Keep it short and non-judgemental. A ignores a real part of the paramedic role. C blames a parent instead of offering a fix, and blame doesn't solve the problem. D is wrong because the report should record objectively whether a helmet was used, not your opinion; that objective fact is exactly what injury surveillance needs.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。这是可教时机：他听得进去，场合平静，而且有具体的办法：戴头盔。说得简短、不评判。A 忽略了院前急救员角色的一个真实部分。C 是在责怪家长而不是给出办法，责怪解决不了问题。D 错在报告应该客观记录是否戴了头盔，而不是你的看法；这个客观事实正是伤害监测需要的。

slides.title: Opioids: the crisis and your safety
slides.body:
• 2016: over 2,800 apparent opioid deaths in Canada
  • BC drug-poisoning deaths: 4.2 → 30.9 per 100,000 (2008 → 2018)
  • Fentanyl in about 84% of BC illicit-drug deaths (2017)
  • Nitrile gloves are enough for routine handling
  • Skin contact: lots of water, no alcohol sanitizer
  • Powder may be airborne: fitted N95 or P100
slides.say: In 2016, there were more than two thousand eight hundred apparent opioid-related deaths in Canada. In BC, the drug-poisoning death rate rose from four point two per hundred thousand in 2008 to thirty point nine in 2018, and fentanyl was found in about eighty-four percent of illicit-drug deaths in 2017. Now your safety, from a 2017 toxicology position statement. Nitrile gloves are enough for routine handling. Brief skin contact is unlikely to poison you, but wash right away with plenty of water, not alcohol sanitizer. If powder could be in the air, wear a fitted N95 or P100. And have naloxone ready.
slides.sayZh: 2016 年，全国有超过两千八百例疑似阿片相关死亡。在 BC，药物中毒死亡率从 2008 年的每十万人四点二，升到 2018 年的三十点九；2017 年约百分之八十四的非法药物中毒死亡检出了芬太尼。再说你的安全，依据 2017 年一份毒理学立场声明：常规接触戴丁腈手套就够了。偶然的皮肤接触不太可能让你中毒，但要立即用大量清水冲洗，不要用酒精洗手液。如果粉末可能飘在空气中，戴合身的 N95 或 P100。还要备好纳洛酮。

slides.title: Building a prevention program
slides.body:
Assess the community→Define the problem→Set goals and objectives
Plan and test→Implement and evaluate
  • SMART: specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, time-sensitive
  • Process objective: how much you did (car seats checked)
  • Outcome objective: what changed (more kids in helmets)
slides.say: To start a community program, the textbook gives five steps. One, assess the community: bring partners together, from police and schools to injured people's families. Two, define the problem with data: who is hurt, where, when, and how. Three, set a broad goal, then SMART objectives: specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-sensitive. A process objective counts what you did, like car seats checked. An outcome objective measures what changed, like how many more children wear helmets. Four, plan the intervention and test it on a small group. Five, implement it and measure results, and keep it going, because effects fade when attention drops.
slides.sayZh: 要在社区启动项目，书里给了五个步骤。一，社区评估：把各方伙伴召集起来，从警察、学校到伤者家属。二，用数据界定问题：谁受伤、在哪里、什么时候、怎么受伤。三，定一个宽泛的目标，再定 SMART 的具体目标：具体、可测量、可达到、现实、有时限。过程目标计算你做了多少，比如检查了多少儿童座椅；结果目标衡量改变了多少，比如多了多少孩子戴头盔。四，计划干预措施，先在小范围试点。五，实施并测量结果，还要坚持下去，因为关注一减少，效果就会回落。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Your PCR is injury data: record facts, not opinions
  • Bad timing or blame wastes the teachable moment
  • Possible fentanyl: gloves on; wash skin with water, not sanitizer
  • Powder in the air? Fitted N95 or P100 before you go in
  • Few calls truly need lights and siren; crashes en route hurt people
  • Practise what you preach: seat belt on, on and off duty
slides.say: First, your patient care report is now injury data, so record facts: the mechanism, the injuries, and whether safety devices were used, not judgements. Second, a teachable moment backfires if the timing is wrong or it sounds like blame. Third, on overdose scenes, wear nitrile gloves; if powder touches your skin, wash with plenty of water, never sanitizer, and if powder could be airborne, put on a fitted N95 or P100 first. Fourth, remember that ambulances speeding to calls cause injuries too, and very few calls truly need lights and siren. Finally, practise what you preach: seat belt on, on and off duty.
slides.sayZh: 第一，你的病人护理报告现在就是伤害数据，所以要记录事实：致伤机制、伤情、是否使用了安全装置，而不是评判。第二，时机不对或听起来像责怪，可教时机就会适得其反。第三，药物过量现场戴丁腈手套；粉末沾到皮肤，用大量清水冲洗，绝不用洗手液；粉末可能飘在空气中时，先戴好合身的 N95 或 P100。第四，记住救护车赶赴现场时同样会撞车伤人，真正需要警灯警笛的呼叫很少。最后，以身作则：无论当班还是下班，都系好安全带。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
Book: have naloxone ready. BC's Suspected Narcotic Overdose protocol adds:

  • Ventilate first: BVM as needed, oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Check blood glucose; correct it if ≤ 4 mmol/L
  • Naloxone IM/IV: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg, reassess every 3 min
  • Or naloxone 4 mg intranasal
  • EMR and PCP both give naloxone
  • PCP adds: IV naloxone if still unconscious and apneic
slides.say: The textbook just says to have naloxone ready. BC's Suspected Narcotic Overdose protocol adds the tested details. Breathing comes first: manage the airway, support ventilations with a bag-valve mask as needed, and give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher. Check the blood glucose, and correct it if it's four or lower. Naloxone starts at zero point four milligrams IM or IV. Every three minutes, if the patient hasn't reached a saturation of ninety-four and breathing above ten, give zero point four, then zero point eight, then two milligrams. Or give four milligrams intranasally. Both EMRs and PCPs give naloxone, but only the PCP has the IV route: if the patient stays unconscious and apneic, consider IV access and IV naloxone.
slides.sayZh: 书里只说要备好纳洛酮。BC 的疑似麻醉药过量流程补充了考试会考的细节。呼吸优先：管理气道，需要时用球囊面罩辅助通气，给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上。测血糖，四或以下就要纠正。纳洛酮从零点四毫克肌注或静注开始。之后每三分钟评估一次，如果病人还没达到血氧九十四、呼吸每分钟十次以上，就依次给零点四、零点八、两毫克；或者经鼻给四毫克。EMR 和 PCP 都可以给纳洛酮，但只有 PCP 能走静脉：病人持续昏迷且呼吸暂停时，考虑开静脉、静脉给纳洛酮。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Primary prevents, secondary limits harm, tertiary rehabilitates
  2. Combine the four Es; passive protection usually works best
  3. As a PCP: teachable moments, factual PCRs, safe overdose scenes

Next: Chapter 4, medical and legal issues
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: primary prevention stops injuries happening, secondary prevention limits the harm, and tertiary prevention is rehabilitation. Two: the four Es, education, enforcement, engineering, and economic incentives, work best together, and passive protection that needs no effort usually works best of all. Three: as a PCP, turn calls into prevention. Use teachable moments with a specific fix, write factual reports that become injury data, and stay safe on overdose calls, ventilating first and giving naloxone the BC way. Next lesson, Chapter 4, we turn to the law: your legal framework, accountability, and scope. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，一级预防阻止伤害发生；二级预防减轻伤害后果；三级预防是康复。二，四个 E——教育、执法、工程、经济激励——组合使用最好，而不需要人付出努力的被动保护通常效果最佳。三，作为 PCP，把出车变成预防：抓住可教时机给出具体办法，写客观的报告成为伤害数据，在过量现场保护好自己，按 BC 的方式先通气、再给纳洛酮。下节课，第四章，我们进入法律：你的法律框架、责任和执业范围。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
